scope: Rust describes all ten preference categories and the 52-row catalogue: native-baseline row order, kinds, keys, descriptions, placeholders, choices, action roles and control copy. The opt-in native adapter consumes that catalogue; browser stores/validation and native interaction/container ownership remain explicit boundaries.

contracts: Rust returns ten category names/descriptions and all 52 original macOS rows in original construction order. The catalogue contains theme/pinned/animation/default-search roles, 22 generic switches, six text fields, five generic selectors, ten navigation/service actions and compound directory/site-editor/site-rules/clear-data/shortcut-hint roles. The opt-in builder selects its rows and control kinds from Rust descriptors. Views retains its original row builder.

Rust owns original row titles/descriptions, registered UI preference keys, numeric choice ordering, text placeholders, save/open/directory accessible names, site editor labels/type order/policy choices and clear-data labels/periods/checkbox copy. Certificates are a native capability fact; disabling that capability removes only its descriptor and leaves all other order/text unchanged.

The native adapter retains actual preference value reading and admitted writes, managed/editable checks, native normalization, per-profile/global scope, directory/password/system-settings/browser services, URL/site-rule validation, data-clearing confirmation, timers, context and persistence. Rust descriptors are UI data and do not authorize arbitrary store keys or platform operations.

Existing Rust text-draft/profile refresh/admission/filter/paging state and existing scene editor/selector/switch/checkbox/action factories remain in use. Profile-specific values and dynamic provider options still come from native services. Compound child containers, native event/focus/AX/menu/scroll/window nodes, header/profile/status/managed copy and remaining busy/service coordination still require migration.

Four Rust regressions cover category/row/control counts and platform gating, exact registered key/kind/order mapping, text/action accessibility and placeholder contracts, and numeric/site/period choice ordering. A shared browser regression compares every original row title/detail/order across all ten categories, checks site labels against native service constants and exercises description-based filtering. Another activates all four tools navigation roles and verifies the actual destination controls and closed preferences window on both backends.

No dependency or browser-service policy was added. Complete interaction/container ownership, other surfaces and full manual/performance/release acceptance remain open. No controlled CPU/GPU/presentation or memory gain is established.
